display_name: 光通信设备/相干光网络/磷化铟光子集成
sub_industry: 光通信设备、相干光网络、磷化铟光子集成与数据中心互联
current_cycle_state: AI cluster and cloud interconnect demand is lifting optical-network orders, especially coherent pluggables, line systems, DSPs, and vertically integrated photonic components. Market pricing is rewarding AI-and-cloud optical exposure, but near-term earnings may lag because capacity, InP fab ramp, and product sampling/volume timing require investment.

primary_anchor.method: EV/Sales or PS with normalized margin bridge
primary_anchor.reason: When AI optical demand is accelerating and earnings are distorted by acquisition integration, fab ramp, R&D, and capacity investment, revenue exposure and credible normalized operating-margin path are more informative than trailing PE alone.

secondary_anchors.reason: Useful once management guidance or normalized margin targets can be defended. For mature telecom equipment portions, normalized profit still matters.
Useful for checking how much premium the market pays for AI optical exposure versus diversified telecom equipment.
Useful when the group combines mature mobile networks, patent licensing, IP routing, optical systems, and InP/PIC optionality.

weak_or_floor_anchors.reason: Book value does not capture DSP, PIC, customer qualification, or optical roadmap value, but it helps identify downside support and balance-sheet strain.
Useful only for mature telecom-equipment cash return, not for valuing the AI optical growth option.

disabled_anchors.reason: Trailing earnings can be depressed by acquisition integration, R&D, fab ramp, restructuring, or one-time tax items and can understate or overstate normalized power.
A series with tax reversals, restructuring, acquisition effects, and cycle troughs should not mechanically determine a growth-stock valuation.

anchor_switch_rationale: The sector has moved from telecom capex replacement-cycle pricing toward AI data-center interconnect pricing. For companies with real optical-network and InP/PIC exposure, the market currently emphasizes AI-cloud order growth, book-to-bill, capacity lead times, vertical integration, DSP/PIC roadmap, and normalized margin bridge. For diversified telecom vendors, SOTP is needed because mobile infrastructure and patent licensing deserve different multiples.
valid_when: AI and cloud optical orders remain strong and book-to-bill is above one
optical-network revenue growth is visibly above group growth
InP/PIC manufacturing ramp improves supply control without material yield failures
new coherent DSP/pluggable/line-system products reach sampling and volume milestones
peer multiples continue to reward AI optical exposure
invalid_when: AI data-center capex slows or optical lead times normalize abruptly
new InP capacity ramp misses yield, cost, or delivery milestones
revenue growth is driven mainly by channel pull-forward rather than repeat cloud demand
customer concentration or hyperscaler bargaining power compresses margins
market valuation language reverts to mature telecom equipment PE/dividend yield
market_pricing_language: EV/Sales or PS versus normalized margin bridge
SOTP discount for diversified telecom exposure
key_cycle_indicators: AI data-center capex and DCI demand
gross margin and operating margin bridge

sources.name: Nokia Q4 2025 and full-year 2025 financial report
Nokia launches application-optimized optical solutions for AI-era networks

analyst_notes: Update quarterly or immediately after Nokia's Q2/Q3 2026 results, a material AI-cloud order revision, optical peer multiple reset, or disclosure of InP fab ramp/yield issues.
